question: A group of pilgrims develops profuse watery diarrhoea 12 hours after eating reheated meat curry at a community kitchen. There is no fever. Which mechanism of food poisoning best fits this presentation?

answers.text: Toxico-infection — organism multiplied in the gut and produced toxin in vivo

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An 8–16 hour incubation with watery diarrhoea but no fever fits toxico-infection (e.g. Clostridium perfringens type A enterotoxin produced during sporulation in gut). The organism must multiply in vivo before releasing toxin, explaining the longer incubation than preformed-toxin poisoning.

answers.text: Intoxication — preformed toxin ingested directly from the contaminated food

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Preformed toxin (intoxication) causes illness within 1–6 hours because the toxin is already active in the food at ingestion. A 12-hour incubation is too long for S. aureus or B. cereus emetic-type poisoning.

answers.text: Infection — invasive organism penetrating the intestinal mucosa causing inflammation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Invasive infection (e.g. Salmonella, Campylobacter) typically has incubation >24 hours, causes fever, and often produces bloody stools — none of which are present here.

Food allergy presents within minutes to hours with urticaria, angioedema, or GI symptoms. Isolated watery diarrhoea at 12 hours affecting a group points to an infective aetiology, not individual allergy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Classify by incubation and fever: 1–6 h without fever = intoxication; 8–16 h without fever = toxico-infection; >24 h with fever = infection/invasion.
The three types differ by incubation: intoxication (1–6 h, preformed toxin), toxico-infection (8–16 h, in vivo toxin), infection (>24 h, invasion + fever).
